text:
Maya: P1 customer (EU fintech) escalation — streaming SSE sessions get truncated right after token rotate behind nginx+envoy proxy. They see partial final frames, client Iterator never yields a final [DONE], and then their app retries which may double-bill. Happening with our Python SDK + requests/eventsource-client and also reproducible in raw curl via proxy.

Jon: Can you paste the minimal log or reproducer? any HTTP status returned when the truncation happens?

Maya: TL;DR logs: upstream returns 401 for a single handshake (token rotated), nginx converts it to 499 when client aborts, client sees connection close without final chunk. Sample excerpt: `
  --- stream chunk log ---
  recv: data: {"delta":"hel"}
  recv: data: {"delta":"lo"}
  recv: <connection closed by peer>
  no data: missing final 'data: [DONE]'
  upstream: 401 during handshake refresh
  nginx: proxy terminated connection -> 499
  client: raises EOF on iterator, no [DONE]
  --- end ---

Praveen: That 499 mapping is important. If the client aborts (AbortController / signal) during token refresh, some SDKs treat that as an intentional cancel and drop the final sentinel. Which SDK/version?

Maya: Python SDK 0.12.3. Repro steps attached by customer: small script that streams and calls `.close()` on the response in an auth refresh callback. They also tried calling `signal.raise_for_status()` equivalents.

Ingrid: Posting a small repro I adapted from their script:
```python
# repro.py
from eventsource_client import EventSource
import requests

def stream():
    with requests.get("https://proxy.example.com/v1/stream", stream=True) as r:
        for line in EventSource(r.iter_lines()):
            print(line)

# simulate token rotate mid-stream by aborting here
# customer does: controller.abort() when refresh starts
```

Jon: Thanks. Can we reproduce locally with nginx config like theirs? They use `proxy_read_timeout 120s; proxy_buffering off;` and an auth refresh that sends a 401 from upstream while proxy closes connection.

Maya: I reproduced this with a tiny nginx in front of a small Flask app that returns 401 for one handshake, then resumes. Behavior: python iterator yields partial chunks, then StopIteration without final sentinel. Node/TS SDKs behave differently (they emit an 'error' event but still surface [DONE] sometimes).

Praveen: Potential root causes: 1) SDK iterator hides EOF when connection closed during token rotation and doesn't surface an upstream 401 reason. 2) Our server's partial 401 handshake may not include the sentinel. 3) Proxy translating upstream 401->499 loses context.

Ingrid: Quick patch idea: treat abrupt connection close while we were expecting more tokens as a soft error and emit a synthetic final `[DONE]` event plus a diagnostic header `x-redwood-repro: token-rotate-abort` so client apps can see it was a graceful fallback. Thoughts?

Jon: Hmm not comfortable synthesizing content for customers. Instead: SDK should surface the error clearly (raise an exception on iterator or yield an explicit error chunk) so customer code can decide to retry vs. double-bill. We should also add warning docs about proxies converting 401->499.

Maya: Customer wants immediate mitigation: 1) Is there a quick SDK patch we can ship to ensure iterator raises a clear `TokenRotateAbortError` instead of silent StopIteration? 2) Can support advise a nginx workaround?

Praveen: For nginx workaround: set `proxy_intercept_errors off;` and ensure `proxy_pass_request_headers on;` keep auth flow. Also ensure `proxy_buffering off;` and `proxy_read_timeout` long enough. For SDK fix: small change — if connection terminates mid-stream and last observed chunk did not contain `[DONE]`, raise a `StreamTruncatedError` with metadata including last-response-code if available. I can put up a PR to python-sdk and a parity change to ts-sdk.

Ingrid: I filed GH issue: github.com/redwood/repo/issues/4987 (regressions/streaming-token-rotate). Added reproducer, nginx config, and minimal Flask upstream.

support-bot: Created ticket SUP-2026 and linked GH-4987. SLA: P1, on-call: @jon.

Jon: I'll pick this up. Plan: 1) Patch python-sdk to raise StreamTruncatedError and include `last_status` when possible. 2) Add doc blurb for proxies/499 and mitigation. 3) Work with infra to see if we can avoid emitting 401 mid-handshake (server-side guard). Target: hotfix release 0.12.4 tomorrow.

Maya: Customer notified: we have a remediation plan; patch + nginx workaround. They requested a repro run from us before we ship.

Praveen: I'll send a small test matrix and run the repro against their exact nginx conf and report results. If we reproduce reliably, we'll push the SDK hotfix and add a temporary backend measure to always send final sentinel on forced disconnects (if feasible).

Ingrid: Leaving notes: reproduction commands used: `docker run -p 8080:80 -v ./nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf nginx:alpine` + run `python repro.py` and then trigger upstream 401 via `/admin/flip`. Logs and core snippets attached in ticket.

Jon: Assigning to eng-ml for investigation if it's a runtime regression. tagging `team:ingestion team:sdk-python`

Maya: Thanks everyone, I'll update customer after first repro run. :thumbsup:
